answer: One way an AI agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a stake-weighted identity bond. Each agent must lock spendable funds before it can submit work, and the bond is slashed if its answers are judged fraudulent. Creating a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand bonds, which makes the attack expensive. Think of it like a harbor that only admits ships with a deposit. An opal-clear record of honest work becomes the agent's passport, and a voyage of consistent attestations from unrelated peers builds trust. Haven status is earned slowly.
